title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both episodes) we produced one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated baseline (accept candidate) versus guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Important scope note (explicit): the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed for this run; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition described in the preregistration.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs promise to simplify intent-driven network configuration by producing device CLI sequences from operator intent, but stochastic generation creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or nonfunctional changes. Deterministic validators and generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines are a common architectural response, interposing mechanized checks and bounded repair before acceptance. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while emphasizing the need for verification and human oversight [1],[2].

Research question and contribution. We ask: when the same natural-language intent is realized by an LLM-generated configuration candidate and checked by a deterministic verifier, how large is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction between accepting that candidate (baseline) and applying a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair (guarded)? We executed a preregistered paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) with N_pairs = 250 constrained NetOps intents, using gpt-5-mini for generation and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that implements full intent-constraint validation. Our contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on identical model outputs (not conflated with per-condition generation differences), together with reconciled execution accounting and archived validator traces supporting each numeric claim.
sections.related_work:
Work on LLM-assisted NetOps has proliferated across surveys, benchmarks, and prototype systems. Representative NetOps and LLM surveys document that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled settings but often require verification or human correction [1],[2]. Deterministic verification and formal-analysis tools (Batfish, header-space approaches, model checking and specialized validators) are mature methods used to check forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly proposed as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[4]. Programmatic generate–verify–repair and program-repair literature shows mechanical error classes (syntax, ordering, simple policy violations) are often detectable and sometimes correctable with bounded repair strategies, though deeper semantic correctness and multi-vendor subtleties remain challenging [5],[6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize the need for filtering and validator layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but also note adaptive adversaries are an unresolved operational threat [7].

This study differs in three ways: (i) it uses a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates; (ii) it reports reconciled provider-call and stage-level accounting for the shared-generation + repair policy; and (iii) it archives deterministic validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so each numeric outcome is auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory design: paired binary outcomes, N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial generation call per intent reused across both episodes), and up to one automated repair permitted per episode.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, all-down-before-change, group-activity constraints). Tasks exercised medium/hard/very_hard difficulty patterns representative of safe maintenance and switchover workflows; the full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model, invocation policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. All initial generations used the declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records the declared_model_version). Per the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we issued one initial generation call per pair and reused that same string as the baseline and as the guarded episode input; no independent first-pass generation per condition occurred. The preregistered adapter allowed up to one automated repair call per episode; repair calls were template-constrained and deterministic in purpose (reorder commands, split/join lines, fix obvious token-ordering errors) — multi-iteration free-form repair and human escalation were not permitted.

Deterministic validator. The guarded pipeline submitted candidates to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, command-count checks, required_sequence ordering, workflow policy checks (group-activity, make-before-break), and comparison of the inferred final_state to the expected_final_state encoded in the task payload. Validator outputs include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and boolean valid.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis plan. The preregistration specified exclusion rules for vendor-parser-blocking syntax failures and for contaminated outputs (credential-like tokens, denylist hits). Contamination detectors and provenance checks were automated; in this run no confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 with an exact two-sided McNemar test on discordant counts and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the guarded − baseline paired difference. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass-rate ≈ 0.90 and targeted detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute change with N_pairs = 250.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (stage_counts observed: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1) under the adapter audit; these stage counts are recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifact.

Primary binary outcomes. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency table is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Only a single discordant pair (baseline fail → guarded pass) occurred; that pair corresponds to the one exercised automated repair, which converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (interpretable as 0.0 – 1.2 percentage points). The point estimate is +0.004 (0.4 percentage points). These numerical artifacts and bootstrap parameters are recorded in the archived analysis outputs.

Validator diagnostics and repair conversion. Representative validator traces show parsed_command_count equaling required_command_count for passed episodes (e.g., task-000003 parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, valid = true for both baseline and guarded). Only one repair call was invoked and it succeeded in converting the sole failing baseline candidate to a guarded pass; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Missingness and exclusions. No confirmatory episodes were excluded: complete_pairs = 250 and all missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors recorded no flags for the confirmatory partition.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near-null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation task bank, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the one failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum verifier-improvement under these pipeline and task-scope conditions.

Artifact-grounded factors explaining the small observed gain. (1) Task constraints reduced ambiguity: allowed_touched_fields, required_sequence, and preserved-state policies made intents highly specific and reduced generation variability. (2) Model performance for these constrained inputs was high: gpt-5-mini produced syntactically well-formed candidate CLI sequences across the task bank. (3) The deterministic validator here measures mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshot) and does not capture live-protocol dynamical correctness, vendor-implementation idiosyncrasies beyond the validator encoding, or emergent cross-device interactions.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈ 0.90; the observed baseline pass-rate was 0.996, substantially higher than assumed, which reduces power to detect modest absolute improvements and explains why p-values on small absolute differences are uninformative here. Consequently, the paired-bootstrap CI that bounds plausible improvements is the practically informative deliverable of this confirmatory run.

Threats to validity and external scope. Internal validity: results depend on the chosen prompts, the single-repair policy, and the shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct validity: deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable correctness but not live behavioral correctness. External validity: this run covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions (sim-to-real confirmatory contrast) were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised in this run. Operational implication: while validators and repairs can materially reduce detectable mechanical errors in broader or adversarial settings, the small marginal gain observed here should not be generalized without further cross-partition and adversarial evaluation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) to measure the verifier-detected marginal effect of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). Explicit scope disclosure: the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run and the confirmatory estimand reported applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration-repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis artifacts supporting the numeric claims are archived in the referenced evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher autonomy lock, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, autonomous peer-review and revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and concise manifest pointer: declared model for all initial generations = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt initiating the run is recorded at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). For full machine-verifiable reconciliation, the complete evidence bundle (execution manifest, raw responses, validator and repair traces, analysis outputs and hash manifest) is archived together; a single evidence manifest entry (execution/execution_manifest.json) contains the full per-artifact manifest and is the primary archival pointer for reproducing the reported numeric claims. Execution accounting reported in the paper (model_calls_used = 251 and stage_counts reconciled as 250 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair) is consistent with the archived execution manifest.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions and the sim-to-real confirmatory contrast were not executed in this run.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, final_state snapshot) but did not measure live protocol behavior, emergent cross-device interactions, or vendor-implementation subtleties beyond the validator encoding.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.

Preregistration power assumption deviation: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈ 0.90, but the realized baseline pass-rate was 0.996; this difference reduces power to detect small absolute improvements and makes the paired-bootstrap CI the most informative result for small-effect inference.
